s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of lower back pain and neurological deficits in the lower extremities following a traumatic event
salient_findings: Lower back pain and tingling sensation radiating to bilateral lower extremities
Rapid progression to bilateral lower-extremity weakness
Abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris
key_facts: Patient is an 18-year-old female
Patient is an experienced volleyball player, yoga practitioner, and weightlifter
Patient presented after her eighth surfing lesson
Initial examination showed 0/5 strength of bilateral lower extremities
Intact sensation and proprioception on initial examination
Follow-up examination showed lower-extremity strength of 1 to 2/5 on MRC scale
Positive Babinski reflex on the right
Clonus bilaterally on follow-up examination
Intact rectal sensation and bowel continence
Classified as L1 American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) C
MRI showed abnormal T2 cord signal from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris
CSF analysis was negative for inflammatory/infectious etiologies
Serum analysis was negative for inflammatory/infectious etiologies

shortlist.label: Spinal cord injury
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of lower back pain and neurological deficits following a traumatic event

shortlist.label: Spinal cord contusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with lower back pain and tingling sensation radiating along the posterior aspect of bilateral lower extremities after a traumatic event

shortlist.label: Conus medullaris syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal T2 cord signal from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris on MRI and bilateral lower-extremity weakness

shortlist.label: Cauda equina syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral lower-extremity weakness and positive Babinski reflex, although intact rectal sensation and bowel continence

shortlist.label: Spinal cord compression
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI and acute onset of neurological deficits in the lower extremities

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including lower back pain, tingling sensation, and bilateral lower-extremity weakness, along with the abnormal T2 cord signal on MRI and the classification as L1 American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) C, are consistent with a spinal cord injury.

rejected.label: Spinal cord contusion
rejected.why: While possible, the term contusion is not as comprehensive as spinal cord injury, which encompasses a broader range of injuries including contusions.

rejected.label: Conus medullaris syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings could suggest involvement of the conus medullaris, but the extent of the injury appears more widespread than what is typically seen in conus medullaris syndrome.

rejected.label: Cauda equina syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's intact rectal sensation and bowel continence, along with the level of injury, do not strongly support cauda equina syndrome.

rejected.label: Spinal cord compression
rejected.why: While compression could be a component of the injury, the term spinal cord injury more accurately describes the patient's condition, which includes both the initial insult and the resulting neurological deficits.
